$comment: Every ui.*/svc.* warning code fails npm run release-check unless an entry here covers it. Entry: {code, reason, match?, max?}. match = regex on the warning message (it cannot cover a lab warning, which has no message); max = total allowed across one gate run. An entry is either a detector false positive (say why the detector is wrong and what judges the real case) or known debt (name the ledger id); debt entries are printed on every run. Delete an entry the day its cause is fixed.

allow.reason: Journeys open views far faster than a person (editor-entry: 20 editors in ~40 s), so one grant passes 60 requests / 5 s. Over-fetching is gated per page view by budgets.maxApiRequestsPerPage instead.
Journeys provoke refusals on purpose (delete-referenced, last-in-boundary, styling dependency) and assert the message themselves. An unexpected refusal fails that journey's own assertion.

The lab logs in, then loads each page cold and reloads it warm: the same document URL three times within 2 s by design. The scale gates log each measured page's fresh browser context in by the same link (O9). A document navigation carries no page-load id, so the service sees one client. Their duplicate API requests are gated per load by the budget block.
Debt (ledger: render-storm, perf#7, perf#3:d): 200-999 ms tasks while the 3.5 MB page parses and ELK lays out. A task of 1 s or more fails.
Lab warnings carry no message, so the 1 s threshold above cannot apply; the lab gates long tasks per load by longTaskMs in lab-budgets.json instead.
Debt: 100-499 ms event-loop stalls (first compiles load Mermaid synchronously; worse on a loaded machine). A stall of 500 ms or more fails: that is work to move off the loop.
The first compile of each family loads its parser (data.cold); at most one per family (seven) per sandbox. A warm slow compile stays gated.

macOS's watcher (FSEvents) reports about four events per atomic rewrite (the temp file made, written and renamed over the target) where Linux's inotify reports about two, and smoke-a-flow-existing commits edits at machine speed, so a burst passes 50 file events in 1 s on a Mac (1 of 3 isolated runs, 2026-11-11; never on Linux CI). The detector itself is right for a real storm (a write loop), which far exceeds max 2 or appears in other runs; that every rewrite is reported once is judged by ts/test/service/watch.test.ts.
